subject: Unexpected 429s during nightly import — mapping mismatch & remediation
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex@greenline.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 22:14:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly import spiking 429s — urgent help requested

Hi Irene,

We started a routine nightly import at ~21:00 PT and for about 18 minutes we're seeing ~35% of requests return 429s. This is impacting the downstream data sync and causing timeouts in our ETL. No code changes on our side.

Key details:
- Import rate: ~2,500 requests/minute (bursty fan-out).
- Time window: 21:03–21:21 PT on 2026-07-20.
- Calls use API key tied to org greenline-prod.

Can you confirm whether this was a quota enforcement action or something on your side? We need a short-term workaround (allowlist? temporary cap bump?) and a root cause so we can communicate to ops.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Green
SRE Lead, Greenline AI

- If this is a policy mismatch we can enable a temporary namespace override to reduce 429s while we remediate.

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Green <alex@greenline.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 01:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly import spiking 429s — urgent help requested

Quick technical summary (initial dig):

What we pulled: serving logs, quota-evaluator traces, routing decisions, and namespace mappings for greenline-prod between 20:45–22:30 PT. Attached a compact log bundle (redwood-logbundle-20260720.tar.gz) to this thread and uploaded raw evidence to Drive.

Preliminary findings:
- Root cause: quota-envelope translation mismatch. A recent routing config change (2026-07-18) introduced a mapping that translated your tenant keys into an intermediate namespace for burst accounting. The translation had an outdated envelope size (1/10th of intended) for the burst window.
- Effect: when your import hit sustained bursts, the quota evaluator computed usage against the smaller envelope and enforced token-level 429s even though overall tenant quota was not exhausted.
- Trigger window aligns exactly with the 21:03–21:21 PT timeframe.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- I pushed a hotfix rule to bypass the translation for greenline-prod at 00:40 PT (this removes the envelope translation and references the canonical tenant envelope). That eliminated further 429s for subsequent imports.

Next steps I propose:
1) Formal rollback of the bad mapping and a test window in staging.
2) Deliver a mapping delta and validation checklist to Greenline (evidence bundle attached).
3) Offer a one-time credit for the impacted window (Monica to propose amount).
4) Create a guardrail in the config pipeline to unit-test envelope translations before rollout.

I'll draft a concise technical summary we can share with your ops team so you can close the loop internally.

- Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Alex Green <alex@greenline.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nightly import spiking 429s — mapping mismatch confirmed + remediation plan

Alex —

Summary for your ops team and next steps below. Short version: we confirmed a config translation error that caused envelope miscalculation and produced the 429s you saw. We've removed the translation and validated that imports proceed without 429s.

What happened (TL;DR):
- A config change added an intermediate namespace translation for burst accounting. The translation was mis-sized (envelope factor 0.1) which caused early enforcement. Not a model or serving capacity failure.

What's included in the attachment bundle:
- redwood-logbundle-20260720.tar.gz: serving traces, quota-evaluator spans (filtered for greenline-prod), and a short timeline.csv.
- remediation-playbook.pdf: steps we used to isolate, bypass, and validate.

Proposed remediation & customer actions:
1) Redwood actions (we've done/plan):
   - Permanent rollback of the translation in config repo (complete).
   - Backfill a unit test for envelope translation in CI (wip, target 2026-08-02).
   - We will issue a usage credit for the impacted 18-minute window; Monica will follow up with the proposed credit and invoice adjustment.
2) Customer actions (suggested, optional):
   - If you want to avoid fan-out spikes during sensitive windows, consider throttling the import's concurrency or staging a rolling import.
   - Validate the attached timeline against your app logs; let us know if timestamps differ.

Monica — can you propose the credit amount and include the accounting/GL references? Alex — please confirm receipt of the attachments and that your ops team has what they need.

Thanks for the patience here; we know 429s in ETL windows are disruptive. We'll treat this as a near-term production reliability improvement in our rollout process.

Irene Choi
